BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material term. It sets the general cap, thresholds, time limits and knowledge bar at levels that would substantially reduce our recovery. It also folds Title and Fundamental claims into the general regime, removes the fraud carve-out, and treats several known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the DD-006 incident, Sandbar) as resolved or immaterial without evidence. We should not accept any of it as drafted. Nothing in the Seller's "FINAL" label or market-context note binds us.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Our playbook | Seller draft | Gap / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 25% / AUD 6.0m start. 20% / AUD 4.8m only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject. Reopen to 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 4.8m figure is a conditional fallback we have no authority to give. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 5,000 | AUD 25,000 | Reject. Five times our figure. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | AUD 250,000, excess only | Reject. See worked example below. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 24 months | 18 months | Reject. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which we have not given. |
| Limitation applies to all Claims (12.3/13) | General regime only | Applies "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Reject. This is a hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits. |
| Title / capacity (Fundamental) | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Reject outright. |
| Fraud carve-out | Carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; non-waivable | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no carve-out | Reject. Insert the carve-out to the maximum enforceable extent. |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure | Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Delete blanket exclusion | Excludes any matter known to Buyer or advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records | Delete. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. |
| Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty's written consent | Reject. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. |
| Riverlark (2 / 7) | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Reject. |
| Bonuses DD-005 (funds flow) | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded | Not itemised; "a matter for the Seller" | Reject. Must be specific or seller-funded. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Reject. Broaden. |
| DD-006 export / privacy (4.6 / Sch 6) | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | "Not expected to be material" | Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require the preservation, investigation and update steps. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Do not accept the characterisation without evidence. Assess; no automatic deduction. |
| Tax / IP | Open; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | "Settled under the general regime" | Reject. Tax and IP are not settled and must stay in separate categories. |
| Title (DD-012) | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is internal and not proof | Share register at DD-012 is the evidence | Reject as sole evidence. |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**Caps, thresholds and time limits (the economic core).** The combined effect of the Seller's terms is substantial. Take aggregate valid claims of AUD 300,000, each above AUD 25,000:
- **Our playbook:** the basket is AUD 50,000, and once exceeded the Seller is liable from the first dollar. We recover AUD 300,000.
- **Seller draft:** claims recover only the excess over AUD 250,000. We recover AUD 50,000.

The Seller's 25,000 de minimis also removes any individual claim below that figure, however many there are. Add the lower cap (AUD 1.2m less headroom) and the shorter 18-month period, and a material share of realistic claims would fall outside recovery.

**Title and Fundamental claims.** Applying general caps and time limits to capacity and title warranties is a structural error, not an administrative simplification. Title is the core of what we are buying. The playbook requires a separate regime at 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. The Seller's "all Claims" limitation language would also override that regime, which the playbook prohibits.

**Fraud carve-out and exclusive remedy.** Without a carve-out, the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses could bar claims for deliberate misconduct or wilful concealment. The playbook treats this as non-waivable.

**Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Read together, clauses 1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7 and 8.3 would mean that anything in the data room, Accounts or public records is disclosed against our warranties and is also treated as known to us. That is a double bar. It would effectively remove warranty protection for the diligence record. Our position is specific disclosure only, and deletion of the blanket knowledge exclusion.

**Bluefen.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). The disclosure confirms the final written consent is not in the record and its conditions (11.2 and 11.3) are not shown to be satisfied. "Satisfied on delivery" would allow Completion before we know whether consent is effective. This needs effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion.

**Riverlark.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unpaid, per the disclosure. A release "following Completion" leaves us holding the risk of the security. The funds flow must pay the current payout directly from Completion funds, with effective releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**Bonuses (DD-005).** The AUD 420,000 is conditional on Completion and continued employment. The Seller's funds flow does not itemise it, and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. Excluding it silently from the funds flow would leave us exposed to a liability we have not priced. It must be either a specific line item or seller-funded, with on-costs included.

**Ironquay IP.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. The data room shows AUD 180,000 open (DD-010), but this is not independent bank verification. We have not verified it either way. The indemnity should be broadened and the SOW3 cure mechanism preserved. Confirmatory assignment and payment evidence should be pre-Completion conditions.

**DD-006 export / privacy incident.** The disclosure describes a download link sent to an unintended external address, with a possible export of about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). It does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion the record does not support. We should not assume a breach, harm or notification duty, and we should not assume none. The required steps are log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Whether a specific indemnity is also warranted is a principal-level decision; the playbook does not address it.

**Sandbar renewals.** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are described as ordinary course, but the disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We should assess them. The playbook prohibits automatic debt classification or automatic price deduction.

**Title evidence.** DD-012 is an internal company register supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof of ownership, and the disclosure itself says the Buyer has not completed its own verification. We need independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Examples include ASIC register extracts, PPSR searches, and transfer documents with evidence of the Seller's authority.

**Points the playbook does not cover.** The Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) and the office lease notification (DD-007) are not addressed in the playbook. The disclosure says neither is expressly a consent requirement for the share sale. We should obtain and check the underlying provisions and seek principal direction before taking a position.

**Process points.**
- The "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened" language is an assertion. Unless we have a record of Amelia Frost's written agreement to these terms, we should not treat them as agreed. Any concession beyond the playbook requires her written authority identifying the draft.
- The clause references are inconsistent across the Seller's documents (for example, Riverlark appears as 2/7, and the knowledge clause as 8.3 alone). We should request a consolidated, cross-checked draft.
- The data-room cut-off is 5.00pm 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. We should request a bring-down disclosure to a current date.

## 3. Recommendations

**Do not accept the Seller's draft.** Respond with a mark-up on the following basis:

1. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. Make no concession to 20% / AUD 4.8m without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
2. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, first-dollar once exceeded.
3. **Time:** 24 months for general claims. Title and Fundamental claims at least six years. Delete "applies to all Claims."
4. **Fundamental / Title:** separate regime at 100% cap, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud and deliberate misconduct:** carve out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, register and public-record deemed disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. No consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases before Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Verify payment status and require confirmatory assignment before Completion.
12. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation and updates. Do not accept "not material." Decide with the principal whether a specific indemnity is warranted.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** reject "settled." Keep these categories open and separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
15. **Title:** require independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, transfer and authority documents). Treat DD-012 as internal only.
16. **Process:** request a consolidated draft with consistent references, a bring-down disclosure to a current date, and the underlying Mossvale and lease provisions. Seek principal direction on the Mossvale and lease points, which the playbook does not address.
